session_spawn.title: Start an agent on a task
session_spawn.description: Start an agent on a task. Creates a session record for the run, an initial log entry naming the provider (agent runner), model and reasoning effort, and a claim reserving the task for that session; committing that starts the agent, so a task a run still going holds refuses the whole request. A task a parked run is waiting on, or whose run a wake has asked for or started, starts nothing: that run gets the instruction, on its own provider, and the answer says so. With wait, returns how the run ended (its brief or final output, and its exit code when recorded) instead of the session id. Returns text in content.body. A wait timeout reports that the run is still running and does not kill it.

task.description: the task to hand to the agent, which the session claims; pass its id or registered name

provider.description: id or registered name of the provider (agent runner); it must use command-line transport

model.description: id or registered name of the model the run uses; optional, by default the model row in the provider's using{model} (the opus alias for Claude). The resolved choice is recorded on the session before launch and passed explicitly to the CLI

persona.description: the persona to carry, by id or name (default: the checkout's persona)

effort.description: the reasoning effort, where the model accepts such a setting

account.description: the account the provider's CLI signs in with, by its id, its directory or the directory's name (`.claude-teams-bob`); by default the offered one further under its weekly pace. Recorded on the session, so every later run uses it too

instruction.description: additional instructions beside the task body, which is the agent’s spec

wait.description: block until the run is over and return how it ended

timeout.description: how long to wait: 45m, 2h, or bare seconds (default 30m)

session_stop.title: Stop a managed session
session_stop.description: Stop a session. A native transcript admits no further steps and reads stopped; an already admitted step may finish. A managed process receives SIGTERM and then SIGKILL if needed. Use session wait to see when it has ended. Returns text in content.body.

session.description: the session to stop; pass its id or registered name

session_wait.title: Wait for a session to end
session_wait.description: Wait for a session to end, then return its brief (or final output) and exit code when recorded, as text in content.body. A session still running when the timeout passes is reported as still running, never killed.

session.description: the session to wait on; pass its id or registered name

timeout.description: how long to wait: 45m, 2h, or bare seconds (default 30m)

session_peek.title: Read the end of a session
session_peek.description: Return the last entries of an agent work session as stored in the graph, plus where it stands: its status, or that it is parked and on what. Returns at most lines entries (40 by default, 256 maximum), with each entry previewed to a few lines (an output to 16,384 characters) and a cut one naming the entry eid that graph_show reads whole, as text in content.body; never the provider’s own log file.

session.description: the session to read; pass its id or registered name

lines.description: how many entries to return, newest last (default 40)

machine_register.title: Register a machine that runs sessions
machine_register.description: Register one of your own machines in this space, lending the agent CLIs it has (claude, codex): the machine, and a provider for each CLI, named `<cli> on <machine>`. A session spawned on one of those providers runs on that machine, with your own sign-in to the CLI, once its runner takes it (`yak start` registers the machine and keeps the runner going). Registering again changes nothing. Returns the machine and provider ids as JSON in content.body.

machine.description: the machine, by the name it was registered under (its hostname, unless `yak start` was given another)

clis.description: the CLIs the machine lends: claude, codex

machine_remove.title: Remove a registered machine
machine_remove.description: Remove one of your registered machines from this space along with the agent CLI providers it lent. Finish work on the machine and stop its runner before retiring it. Session transcripts are kept. Returns text in content.body.

machine.description: the name it was registered under (its hostname, unless `yak start` was given another)

session_take.title: Take the next session asked of a machine
session_take.description: Take the oldest session asked of one of your machines' providers that has not run yet, or whose run ended and was asked to carry on, and mark it taken. Returns what to run as a JSON code block in content.body (session, name, cli, instruction, and model, effort and thread where set), or an empty body when nothing is asked. A machine's runner calls it; `session_log` hands back the run.

machine.description: the machine, by the name it was registered under (its hostname, unless `yak start` was given another)

session_log.title: Hand back a machine's run of a session
session_log.description: Read lines a machine's CLI printed for a session it took into the session's transcript, numbered from `from`; with `pid`, record the process; with `exit`, end the run: the exit code (null when it was not seen), an ending entry, and the run's report as a comment on its task. Only the owner of the machine a session was asked of hands back its lines. Returns text in content.body.

machine.description: the machine, by the name it was registered under (its hostname, unless `yak start` was given another)

lines.description: the CLI's output lines, each one JSON object, as printed

from.description: the number of the first of `lines` in the run's output, from 0

pid.description: the CLI's process id on the machine

exit.description: the CLI's exit code, once it ended; null when its end was seen and its code was not

spawn_complete.description: publish the final report on the task and deliver it to the spawning session after a managed run’s final log import

spawn_start.description: start the run a session asks for: a `using` written on an entry names the provider, the model and the effort

spawn_stop.description: kill the run a `stop` on the session running it names
